questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Stretch and Vertical Shift of a Transformed Cotangent Curve
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007410/assets/454c2746d17f6444a9fa5762baae3927fb72eff6a7e51a1df38bc4f325a4a830.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
questions.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{2\pi }{3}-0=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{2\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{2\pi }{3})}=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $2$ units up. Hence, $D=2.$

Therefore, $B+D=\frac{3}{2}+2=\frac{7}{2}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})+2.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007410/assets/5819e0605dacfb190c2767c4f50a671eb592832aa6a3a1970a8bcdff2790fd19.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+C) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(3(x+\frac{C}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3(x+\frac{C}{3}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007410/assets/ad5bf0001a37cf5bebf3288ffbf1fa6bb69747f28f8a81d08d0ffab8223e1707.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)$ by $\frac{\pi }{21}-0=\frac{\pi }{21}$ units to the right. Therefore

$$
\frac{C}{3}=-\frac{\pi }{21}\,⟹\,C=-\frac{\pi }{7}.
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $-\frac{\pi }{7}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\frac{\pi }{7}.$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007410/assets/f86984919b15283134e1b3a9479ff8c79ec8dfacc84975e82f88704b7b26dd3a.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is  $B-2D?$
questions.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{4}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{\pi }{4})}=4.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $\frac{9}{4}$ unit down. Therefore, $D=-\frac{9}{4}.$

Therefore, $B-2D=4-2\cdot (-\frac{9}{4})=4+\frac{9}{2}=\frac{17}{2}.$  

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(4x)-\frac{9}{4}.
$$
